items.stem: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have similar chemical properties mainly because they have the same...

options.text: Number of electrons in their outer shell
options.rationale: Correct: the same number of outer electrons gives similar reactions.
Neutron number varies and does not set group behaviour.
Mass increases down a group; it does not define the group.
Colour is not what groups elements together.

items.explanation: Correct: the same number of outer electrons gives similar reactions.

options.text: Reactivity increases going down Group 1 (alkali metals)
options.rationale: Correct: alkali metals get more reactive down the group.
Correct: halogens get less reactive down the group.
Group 1 reactivity increases down the group.

options.text: All groups react in exactly the same way

items.stem: How does the periodic table help a scientist who finds an unfamiliar element in Group 1?

options.text: They can predict it will be a reactive metal that behaves like other alkali metals
options.rationale: Correct: position predicts properties, so Group 1 means a reactive alkali metal.

options.text: They can tell its exact price
options.rationale: The table does not give prices.

options.text: They learn nothing about its behaviour
options.rationale: Position in the table predicts properties.

options.text: They know it must be a non-metal
options.rationale: Group 1 elements are metals, not non-metals.

items.explanation: Correct: position predicts properties, so Group 1 means a reactive alkali metal.
